Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 1:

Surat al-Hajj (Sura of the Pilgrimage) [Meccan, except for "And among the people is he who worships Allah..." the two verses, or "These two adversaries..." the six verses, which are Medinan. Its verses number 78. It was revealed after Surat an-Nur (The Light).]

﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah and others, ﴿fear your Lord﴾, i.e., His punishment, by obeying Him, ﴿indeed, the convulsion of the Hour﴾, i.e., the violent shaking of the earth, after which the sun will rise from its west, which is the nearness of the Hour, ﴿is a thing tremendous﴾ in terrifying people, which is a kind of punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 2:

﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed﴾ (tadhhal), by reason of it (bi-sababiha), ﴿every nursing mother﴾ (kullu murdi'ah) in actuality (bi-l-fi'l), ﴿from what she nursed﴾, i.e., she will forget it (tansahu). ﴿And every pregnant one will drop her load﴾, i.e., her fetus (hublā). ﴿And you will see people as drunkards﴾ from the intensity of fear, ﴿but they are not drunkards﴾ from wine. ﴿But the punishment of Allah is severe﴾, so they fear it.

It was revealed concerning an-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his companions: "And among mankind is one who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge" (﴿And among mankind is one who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge﴾). They said: the angels are the daughters of Allah, the Qur'an is the fables of the ancients, and they denied resurrection and the bringing back to life of one who has become dust. "And follows" (﴿And follows﴾) in his disputation "every rebellious devil" (﴿every rebellious devil﴾), i.e., one who is obstinately defiant (mutamarrid).

The commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 4:

﴿It was decreed concerning him﴾ — i.e., it was decided against the Devil (quḍiya ʿalā al-shayṭān) — ﴿that whoever takes him as an ally﴾ — i.e., follows him — ﴿then he will mislead him and guide him﴾ — i.e., he will call him — ﴿to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ — i.e., the Fire.

"O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection (ba'th), [consider that] We created you" — i.e., the people of Makkah — "if you are in doubt" — in suspicion — "about the resurrection, then indeed We created you" — i.e., your origin, Adam — "from dust; then" — We created his descendants — "from a drop" — semen (manī) — "then from a clinging clot" — which is congealed blood — "then from a lump of flesh," which is a piece of flesh the size of what can be chewed, "formed and unformed" — shaped, fully formed in creation — "and unformed," i.e., not fully formed in creation. "That We may make clear to you" — the perfection of Our power, so that you may draw inference from it regarding the initiation of creation, concerning its return — "and We cause to remain in the wombs whom We will for an appointed term" — this is a new clause (mustaʼnaf) — until the time of its emergence. "Then We bring you forth" — from the bellies of your mothers — "as infants" — meaning, as children (aṭfālan). "Then" — We let you grow — "that you may reach your maturity (ashudd)" — i.e., full strength and vigour, which is what lies between thirty and forty years. "And among you is he who is caused to die" — dies before reaching maturity — "and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age" — the lowest of it, from senility and dotage — "so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing." ʿIkrimah said: whoever recites the Qur'an will not come to this state. "And you see the earth lifeless" — dry — "but when We send down water upon it, it stirs" — moves — "and swells" — rises and increases — "and it grows of every fine pair" — kind — "beautiful" — pleasing.

﴿That﴾, referring to what was mentioned, from the beginning of the creation of man to the final revival of the earth, ﴿is because﴾, by reason of the fact that ﴿God, He is the Truth﴾, the Established, the Everlasting.
﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it﴾, [i.e.,] no doubt ﴿about it﴾, ﴿and that Allah will raise up those who are in the graves﴾. It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 8:

﴿And among mankind is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾ with him, ﴿and no illuminating Book﴾ for him, having light with him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 22, verse 9:

﴿Turning aside his side﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning twisting his neck in arrogance against faith. The ʿiṭf (ʿiṭf, the side) is the flank, to the right or to the left. ﴿To mislead﴾ is read with the yā' (ya) either vowelled with a fatḥa or with a ḍamma. ﴿From the way of Allah﴾, meaning His religion. ﴿For him in this world is disgrace﴾, meaning punishment, so he was killed on the Day of Badr. ﴿And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning﴾, meaning burning in the Fire. And it is said to him:

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 10:

﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward.﴾ I.e., what you sent forward. He expressed it by "hands" (yadāk) specifically, rather than other things, because most actions are carried out by them.

﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ I.e., not one who wrongs (bi-dhī ẓulm), ﴿to the servants﴾, so that He would punish them without a sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 11:

﴿And among mankind is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾, i.e., with doubt in his worship, likened to one who stands on the edge of a mountain, for lack of steadiness. ﴿If good befalls him﴾, health and safety in his person and his wealth, ﴿he is reassured by it﴾. ﴿But if a trial befalls him﴾, affliction and sickness in his person and his wealth, ﴿he turns back on his face﴾, i.e., he returns to disbelief. ﴿He loses the world﴾, by the failure of what he hoped to gain from it, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, by disbelief. ﴿That is the manifest loss﴾, the clear one.

﴿He calls upon﴾, that is, worships, ﴿besides Allah﴾, namely the idol, ﴿that which does not harm him﴾ if he does not worship it, ﴿and that which does not benefit him﴾ if he worships it. ﴿That﴾ calling, that is, that supplication, ﴿is the far-reaching error﴾ away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 13:

﴿يَدْعُو لَمَن﴾ [The particle] lam is extra (zā'idah) — ﴿ضَرّه﴾ "whose harm" [comes] from worshipping him — ﴿أقْرَب مِن نَفْعه﴾ "is closer than his benefit," if he benefits by his imagining [it so] — ﴿لَبِئْسَ المَوْلى﴾ "Surely wretched is the patron (al-mawla)," i.e., the helper (al-nāṣir), [that is] he — ﴿ولَبِئْسَ العَشِير﴾ "and wretched is the companion (al-'ashīr)," the associate, [that is] he. Then he followed the mention of the doubter with loss by the mention of the believers with reward, in

﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ — from the obligatory and the voluntary acts — ﴿into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills﴾ — of honouring whoever obeys Him and humiliating whoever disobeys Him.

﴿Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him﴾, that is, Muhammad, His Prophet, ﴿in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch a rope﴾ (with a cord) ﴿up to the sky﴾, that is, to the ceiling of his house, tying it there and to his neck, ﴿then let him cut off﴾, that is, let him strangle himself with it by cutting himself off from the ground, as in al-Sihah. ﴿Then let him see whether his scheming removes﴾ (in not helping the Prophet) ﴿that which enrages him﴾. Its meaning is: let him choke with rage over it, for there is no escape from it.

﴿وكَذَلِكَ﴾ أي مِثْل إنزالنا الآيةَ السابقةَ ﴿أنْزَلْناهُ﴾ أي القرآنَ الباقيَ ﴿آيات بَيِّنات﴾ ظاهراتٍ، حالٌ (ḥāl, circumstantial accusative) ﴿وأَنَّ اللَّه يَهْدِي مَن يُرِيد﴾ هُداهُ مَعْطوفٌ (ma'ṭūf, conjoined) على هاءِ أنْزَلْناهُ

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews,﴾ they are the Jews. ﴿and the Sabians,﴾ a group of them. ﴿and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated partners (with God),﴾ ﴿indeed, God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection,﴾ by admitting the believers into Paradise and admitting others into the Fire. ﴿Indeed, God is Witness over all things,﴾ regarding their deeds, ﴿Witness,﴾ knowing of them with knowledge of direct observation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 18:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ [i.e., do you not know] ﴿that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the moving creatures﴾ [i.e., submits to Him by what is intended of it], ﴿and many among the people﴾ [and they are the believers, with an addition to mere submission, namely the prostration of prayer], ﴿and many deserve the punishment﴾ [and they are the disbelievers, because they refused the prostration that depends on faith] ﴿And whoever Allah humiliates﴾ [i.e., makes wretched], ﴿none can honor him﴾ [none can make him happy]. ﴿Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴾ [of humiliation and honor].

"These two are two adversaries (khasmān) who dispute concerning their Lord." The believers are one adversary (khaṣm), and the five disbelievers are another adversary (khaṣm); the word khaṣm is applied to both the singular and the plural. ﴿They dispute concerning their Lord﴾, i.e., concerning His religion. ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, which they will wear, meaning the fire will encompass them. ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads﴾, the water (al-ḥamīm) that has reached the utmost degree of heat.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 20:

﴿Whereby⁠ what is in their bellies will be melted﴾ (yuṣhar): melted (yudhāb) ﴿by it﴾, ﴿what is in their bellies﴾ of fat and other things, ﴿and﴾ ﴿the skins﴾ (al-julūd) will be scorched (tushwā) by it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 22, verse 21:**

﴿And for them are maqami' (iron hooks/rods) of iron﴾ to strike their heads.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 22:

﴿Whenever they wish to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾ — i.e., the Fire — ﴿out of distress﴾ that overtakes them therein — ﴿they will be returned into it﴾, sent back into it by the iron hooks (al-maqami‘, sing. miq‘ama, iron rods used to strike) — ﴿and﴾ it will be said to them, ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾ — i.e., the punishment that has reached the utmost extent of burning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 23:

And He said concerning the believers: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ — read with the genitive (bi-l-jarr), meaning "of gold and of pearls," i.e., by setting the pearls in gold; and read with the accusative (bi-l-nasb), as a conjunction (ʿatf) on the place (maḥall) of "min asāwir" (bracelets). ﴿And their clothing therein will be silk﴾ — it is that which is forbidden for men to wear in this world.

﴿And they were guided﴾ in this world ﴿to the good speech﴾, which is ﴿there is no god but Allah﴾, ﴿and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the path of Allah, the praiseworthy, and His religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾ [i.e., from His obedience] ﴿and from the Sacred Mosque which We have made﴾ a place of rites (manasik) and worship (muta'abbad) ﴿for the people, equal [in right] are the one who resides there and the one who comes from outside﴾ [i.e., the visitor (al-ta'ri')] ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation [from the truth]﴾ [the ba' in bi-ilhad is extra (za'idah)] ﴿through wrongdoing﴾ [i.e., because of it], by committing something forbidden, even if he insults a servant ﴿We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾ [painful (mu'lim)]: [i.e., part of it]. And from this is derived the predicate of inna: [i.e., We will make them taste of a painful punishment].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 26:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when We settled﴾ for Abraham ﴿the place of the House﴾ (a house) ﴿for Abraham, the place of the House﴾, so that he might build it. It had been lifted up during the time of the Flood. And We commanded him ﴿not to associate anything with Me, and purify My House﴾ from idols ﴿for those who circle it, and those who stand﴾ in devotion there, ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾, the plural of rāki' (one who bows) and sājid (one who prostrates): those who pray.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 27:

﴿And proclaim﴾ (i.e., call out) ﴿among the people the pilgrimage (al-Hajj)﴾. So he called out from the mountain of Abu Qubays: "O people, indeed your Lord has built a House and has made the pilgrimage to it obligatory upon you, so respond to your Lord," and he turned with his face to the right, the left, the east and the west. Everyone whom it was decreed for to perform the pilgrimage from the loins of men and the wombs of mothers responded: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am." The answer to the command is ﴿they will come to you on foot﴾, i.e., walking, plural of rajil, like qa'im and qiyam (standing), ﴿and on every lean camel﴾, i.e., riding, a lean camel (ḍāmir), which is applied to both male and female, ﴿they will come﴾, i.e., the lean camels, taking the meaning into account (ḥamlan 'ala al-ma'na), ﴿from every deep ravine (fajj 'amiq)﴾, i.e., a distant path.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 28:

﴿That they may witness﴾ i.e., attend, ﴿benefits for them﴾ in this world through trade, or in the Hereafter, or in both; there are opinions. ﴿And mention the name of Allah on known days﴾ i.e., the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, or the Day of Arafah, or the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) up to the end of the days of Tashriq; there are opinions. ﴿Over what He has provided for them of the cattle, the camels, cows and sheep, which are slaughtered on the day of the Eid and after it, of the offerings (hadaya) and sacrifices (dahaya)﴾ ﴿So eat from them﴾ if they are recommended to be eaten, ﴿and feed the miserable, the poor﴾ i.e., the one most severely in need.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 29:

﴿Then let them end their state of unkemptness (tafath)﴾, i.e., let them remove their dirt and disheveled hair, such as trimming the nails. ﴿And let them fulfill their vows﴾ — with light and with intensive pronunciation of the verb (al-takhfif wa'l-tashdid) — ﴿concerning the offerings and sacrifices﴾. ﴿And let them circumambulate﴾ the circumambulation of return (tawaf al-ifadah) ﴿around the Ancient House﴾, i.e., the ancient one, because it is the first House that was set up for the people.

﴿That﴾ is a predicate of an implied subject: i.e., the matter or affair is that which has been mentioned. ﴿And whoever honours the sacred rites of Allah﴾, these being what is not lawful to violate, ﴿it is better for him with his Lord﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿And the cattle have been made lawful for you﴾ to eat after slaughter, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ as prohibited in ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion﴾ (Qur'an 5:3), and so the exception is disjunctive (munqati'). It is also permissible that it be connected (muttasil), and the prohibition is due to what occurs of death and the like. ﴿So shun the abomination of idols﴾ — min here is explanatory (li-l-bayan), meaning the abomination that is the idols; ﴿and shun the word of falsehood﴾, i.e., association of partners with Allah in your talbiyah (the chant of the pilgrimage), or false testimony.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 31:

﴿Hunafā’ lillāh﴾ (inclining to God), i.e., Muslims, turning away from every religion other than His religion, ﴿not associating anything with Him﴾: this is an emphasis of what precedes it, and both are circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) referring to the waw (the pronoun of the plural subject). ﴿And whoever associates partners with God, it is as if he had fallen﴾ (kharra), i.e., fallen (saqaṭa) ﴿from the sky, and the birds snatch him away﴾ (fa-takhṭafuhu al-ṭayr), i.e., seize him swiftly, ﴿or the wind throws him﴾ (aw tahwī bihi al-rīḥ), i.e., casts him down ﴿into a far-off place﴾ (makān saḥīq), i.e., distant, so that there is no hope of his deliverance.

﴿That﴾: the word *al-amr* (the matter) is understood before it as its *mubtada'* (subject).

﴿And whoever honours the symbols of Allah, indeed it﴾: i.e., indeed the honouring of them, and they are the camels (*al-budn*) that are sent as offerings to the Haram, by choosing them to be good and well-fed, is from the piety of the hearts of those [who do so]. They are called *sha'a'ir* (symbols) because they are marked (*ish'ar*) with that by which it is known that they are an offering, such as stabbing iron into their humps.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 22, verse 33:

﴿For you there are benefits in them,﴾ such as riding them and loading them with what does not harm them, ﴿until a specified term﴾ meaning the time of their slaughter, ﴿then their place of sacrifice﴾ that is, the place where their slaughter is permitted, ﴿is at the Ancient House﴾ that is, near it, and what is intended is the whole of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 34:

﴿For every community We have appointed rites﴾, i.e., a community of believers that came before you. ﴿That they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle﴾ at the time of slaughtering them. ﴿So your God is one God; so submit to Him﴾, i.e., submit in obedience. ﴿And give good tidings to the humble ones﴾, i.e., the obedient and the humble.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 22, verse 35:**

﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾ fear, ﴿and the patient over what afflicts them﴾ of tribulations, ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾ at its appointed times, ﴿and spend out of what We have provided for them﴾ give in charity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 36:

﴿And the camels⁠ —⁠ﵟ﴾ plural of badanah, which is the camel: ﴿We have made them for you among the symbols of Allah⁠﴾ the markers of His religion ﴿for you therein is good⁠﴾ benefit in this world, as has preceded, and a reward in the Hereafter ﴿so mention the name of Allah over them⁠﴾ at the time of slaughtering them ﴿standing⁠﴾ standing on three legs, with the left forelimb tied ﴿then when they have fallen on their sides⁠﴾ they have collapsed to the ground after slaughter, and this is the time for eating from them ﴿then eat from them⁠﴾ if you wish ﴿and feed the contented⁠﴾ the one who is content with what is given to him and does not ask or approach for it ﴿and the beggar⁠﴾ the one who asks or approaches ﴿thus⁠﴾ meaning, like this subjugation ﴿We have subjected them to you⁠﴾ so that you can slaughter and ride them, for otherwise you would not be able to manage them ﴿that you may be grateful⁠﴾ for My favour upon you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 37:

﴿Their flesh will not reach Allah, nor their blood, but it is piety from you that reaches Him.﴾ Meaning: they are not raised up to Him. ﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾ — meaning: from you, the righteous deed purified for Him, together with faith, is raised up to Him. ﴿Thus He has subjected them to you, that you may magnify Allah for having guided you﴾ — He guided you to the landmarks of His religion and the rites of His pilgrimage. ﴿And give good tidings to the muhsinun (those who do good)﴾ — meaning: the muwahhidun (those who affirm the oneness of Allah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 38:

﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed﴾ [from the plots of the polytheists], ﴿indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ungrateful one﴾ [treacherous] in his trust [ungrateful] for His blessing, and they are the polytheists. The meaning is that He will punish them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 39:

﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against﴾, i.e., to the believers, that they may fight. This is the first verse revealed concerning jihad (struggle, armed striving in the way of God). ﴿Because they have been wronged﴾, i.e., because of the fact that they have been wronged, through the wrongdoing of the disbelievers against them.

(They are) those who have been expelled from their homes without right — in the expulsion, they were not expelled [for any reason] except that they say: "Our Lord is Allah" — alone. And this statement is true, so expelling them because of it is expulsion without right. ﴿And had it not been for Allah's repelling of some people by means of others﴾ — "some" is a substitute for "people" — ﴿they would have been demolished﴾ — with the doubled consonant (tashdid) for intensification, and without it (takhfif) — ﴿monasteries﴾ for monks, ﴿and churches﴾ (bi'a) meaning churches for Christians, ﴿and synagogues﴾ (salawat) meaning churches for Jews, in Hebrew, ﴿and mosques﴾ for Muslims, ﴿in which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾ — i.e., the places mentioned — and acts of worship would cease with their ruin. ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ — i.e., who support His religion. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong﴾ over His creation, ﴿Mighty﴾, unassailable in His dominion and His power.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 41:

﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land,﴾ by giving them victory over their enemy, ﴿they establish the prayer, give the zakat, enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil.﴾ The answer of the conditional clause is this, and it together with its answer is the relative clause (silah) of the relative pronoun; and before it one should supply "hum" (they) as the subject of a nominal sentence (mubtada'). ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of all affairs.﴾ That is, to Him is their return in the Hereafter.

Here is the translation of the passage:

﴿And if they deny you﴾ to the end of the verse: in it is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Then the people of Noah had denied before them﴾ the feminine form of "qawm" (people) is used in view of the meaning. ﴿And ʿĀd﴾ the people of Hud, ﴿and Thamud﴾ the people of Salih.

And the people of Madyan (the people of Shu'ayb), and Musa was denied; he was denied by the Copts, not by his own people, the Children of Israel. That is, these (peoples) denied their messengers, so you have an example in them. ﴿So I gave the disbelievers respite﴾, I granted them time by delaying the punishment for them. ﴿Then I seized them﴾ with the punishment. ﴿So how was My disapproval?﴾ That is, My rejection of them for their denial, by destroying them. The interrogative is for affirmation: that is, it has befallen its proper place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 45:

﴿So how many﴾, i.e., how many (kam), ﴿a town have We destroyed﴾ — and in another reading, "destroyed it" (ahlaktuha) — ﴿while it was wrongdoing﴾, i.e., its people through their disbelief, ﴿so it is fallen﴾, i.e., collapsed, ﴿upon its roofs﴾, i.e., its ceilings. ﴿And﴾ how many ﴿a well left unused﴾, abandoned through the death of its people, ﴿and a lofty palace﴾, high and raised, empty through the death of its owner.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 46:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind.﴾ [Translation of the Qur'anic text in the passage as given.] Hearts with which they understand what befell those who denied before them; ﴿or ears with which they hear﴾ their news of destruction and the ruin of their dwellings, so that they might take warning. ﴿For indeed﴾ that is, the matter (al-qissah) ﴿is not the eyes that go blind﴾ ... ﴿but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾: an emphasis (ta'kid).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 47:

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will never fail His promise﴾ — by sending down the punishment; so He sent it down on the Day of Badr.

﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ — of the days of the Hereafter, on account of the punishment; ﴿like a thousand years of what you count﴾ — read with the ta' (you) and the ya' (they) — in this world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 48:

﴿And how many a town did I give respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it. And to Me is the final return.﴾ The intended meaning is its people. ﴿And to Me is the final return﴾: the return (al-maṣīr, "the final destination").

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 22 (al-Hajj), verse 49:

﴿Say, "O mankind﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿indeed, I am to you a clear warner﴾, one who makes the warning plain, ﴿and a bringer of good news to the believers.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 50:

﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them there is forgiveness﴾ from the sins, ﴿and a generous provision﴾ which is the Garden (al-Jannah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 51:

﴿And those who strive against Our verses﴾ — [striving] to nullify the Qur'an by [attacking] them, ﴿seeking to frustrate [them]﴾ — [i.e., those] who follow the Prophet; that is, they attribute to them incapacity and discourage them from faith, or [they think of] themselves as ones who can outdo Us, ﴿seeking to frustrate [Us]﴾ [i.e., thinking] We are unable to overcome them. In another reading, ﴿Mu'ajjizin﴾ [is read as] "outpacing Us" (musabiqin lana), meaning they suppose they can escape Us by denying the resurrection and the punishment. ﴿They are the companions of the Blaze﴾ — the Fire.

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger﴾ — he is a prophet who was commanded to convey (*tabligh*, the conveying of the message) — ﴿nor any prophet﴾, i.e., one who was not commanded to convey — ﴿except when he wished﴾ — recited — ﴿Satan threw into his wish﴾ — his recitation — what is not from the Qur'an, of what the people to whom he was sent would approve. The Prophet (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Najm before an assembly of Quraysh, after: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ — by Satan's casting onto his tongue, without his (ﷺ) knowledge of it: "Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for." So they rejoiced at that. Then Jibril informed him of what Satan had cast onto his tongue of that, so he grieved, and he was consoled with this verse so that he would be reassured. ﴿Then Allah abrogates﴾ — nullifies — ﴿what Satan casts. Then Allah makes His verses firm﴾ — confirms them — ﴿and Allah is Knowing﴾ of Satan's casting what has been mentioned, ﴿Wise﴾ in His allowing him to do so, by doing what He wills.

﴿So that He may make what Satan throws in a trial﴾ (*miḥnah*, a test) ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ (*shiqāq* wa-*nifāq*, opposition and hypocrisy) ﴿and whose hearts are hardened﴾, meaning the polytheists, against accepting the truth. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿are in a far-reaching schism﴾, a long-standing opposition, with the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, since a mention of their gods was recited upon his tongue in a way that pleased them, and then that was nullified.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 54:

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it [i.e., the Qur'an] is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humbly submit to it.﴾ [They may know] the Tawhid (Oneness of God) and the Qur'an. [Humbly submit] means be at rest (tatma'inn). ﴿And indeed, Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path﴾ [i.e., a path] of way (tariq), ﴿straight﴾, i.e., the religion of Islam.

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt﴾ about it, i.e., the Qur'an, because of what Satan cast onto the tongue of the Prophet, and then it was annulled. ﴿Until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., the hour of their death, or the Resurrection, unexpectedly. ﴿Or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day﴾. It is the day of Badr, in which there was no good for the disbelievers, like the barren wind that brings no good. Or it is the Day of Resurrection, after which there is no night.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 56:

﴿The dominion on that Day﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone, and what it implies of being established is the regent of the adverbial phrase ﴿He will judge between them﴾, between the believers and the disbelievers, by what He will make clear after it, ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss﴾, as a favor from Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 57:

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those will have a humiliating punishment﴾ severe, because of their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 58:

﴿Those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾ i.e., in obedience to Him, from Mecca to Medina, ﴿then were killed or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision﴾ it is the provision of Paradise, ﴿and indeed Allah is the best of providers﴾ the most excellent of givers.

﴿Surely He will admit them to an admission﴾ — read with a damma or a fatha on the mim — that is, an admitting, or a place, ﴿which they will be pleased with﴾, and it is Paradise. ﴿And indeed Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their intentions, ﴿Forbearing﴾ regarding their punishment.

The matter is as We have related to you. ﴿And whoever retaliates﴾ meaning, repays, from among the believers, ﴿with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾ wrongfully by the polytheists, i.e., he fought them as they had fought him in the sacred month, ﴿and then is wronged﴾ by them, i.e., is wronged by being expelled from his home, ﴿Allah will surely help him.﴾ ﴿Indeed Allah is Pardoning﴾ toward the believers ﴿and Forgiving﴾ of them for their fighting in the sacred month.

That (is the victory), because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night (i.e., He makes each of them enter into the other, by lengthening one with the other), and that is a effect of His power, by which victory comes. ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of the supplication of the believers, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of them, in that He placed faith within them, so He answered their supplication.

That (victory) also (is so) because Allah is the Truth, the established (reality), and because what they invoke besides Him, (that is, they worship besides Him,) which is the idols, is the falsehood, the perishing (thing); and because Allah is the Most High (al-ʿAliyy), i.e., the one exalted above everything in His power, the Great (al-Kabir), the One before whom everything other than Him is diminished.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 63:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ that is, do you not know, ﴿that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾ rain, ﴿and the earth becomes green﴾ with vegetation, and this is from the effect of His power. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾ toward His servants in bringing forth vegetation by means of water, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with what is in their hearts at the delay of the rain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 64:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, by way of ownership, ﴿and indeed, Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His servants, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ to His allies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 65:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ (i.e., known) ﴿that Allah has subjected to you what is on the earth﴾ of livestock ﴿and the ship﴾ (i.e., the ships) ﴿running upon the sea﴾ for riding and carrying ﴿by His command﴾ (i.e., by His permission) ﴿and He holds back the sky﴾ from ﴿falling upon the earth, except by His permission﴾ (i.e., lest it fall, so that you would perish). ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful toward mankind﴾ in subjecting and holding back.

And He is the One who gave you life [by bringing you into being], then causes you to die when your terms come to an end, then gives you life again [at the Resurrection]. Indeed, man [i.e., the polytheist] is truly ungrateful for the favours of Allah, by abandoning His Oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 67:

﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak), which they perform.﴾ (It is read with a fatha or a kasra on the sin.) Shari'ah (a sacred law or way of worship). ﴿They are the ones who perform it.﴾ Acting upon it. ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾ — meaning: do not dispute with them. ﴿concerning the matter﴾, that is, the matter of the slaughtered animal, since they said: "Is what Allah has killed not more deserving that you eat it than what you have killed yourselves?" ﴿And invite to your Lord﴾ — to His religion. ﴿Indeed, you are upon guidance﴾ — religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 68:

﴿And if they dispute with you﴾ concerning the matter of the religion, ﴿then say: "Allah knows best what you do"﴾, so that He will recompense you for it. And this was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 69:

﴿Allah will judge between you﴾ O believers and disbelievers ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾ by each of the two groups saying the opposite of what the other says.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 70:

﴿Did you not know﴾ The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir) ﴿that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed that﴾ i.e., what has been mentioned ﴿is in a Book﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) ﴿Indeed that﴾ i.e., the knowledge of what has been mentioned ﴿is easy for Allah﴾, simple.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 71:

﴿And they worship﴾, i.e., the polytheists, ﴿besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, which is the idols, ﴿authority﴾ meaning proof, ﴿and that of which they have no knowledge﴾ that they are gods. ﴿And for the wrongdoers﴾ by associating partners with Allah ﴿there will be no helper﴾ who can prevent from them the punishment of Allah.

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾ from the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾ and manifest in their state, ﴿you will recognize in the faces of those who disbelieved the denial﴾, i.e., the denial of them, meaning its effect of aversion and frowning. ﴿They almost lunge at those who recite Our verses to them﴾, i.e., they fall upon them with violence. ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾ Something more hateful to you than the Qur'an being recited to you: it is ﴿the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieved﴾, that your destination is toward it, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, it.

O people, a parable is presented, so listen to it: Indeed those you invoke besides Allah (i.e., other than Him, and they are the idols) will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose. (Dhubab is a collective noun whose singular is dhubaba, and it applies to both the masculine and the feminine.) And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not recover it from it. (Yastanqidhu-hu means they could not retrieve it.) Because of their weakness, how then do they worship the partners of Allah, the Exalted? This is a strange matter, which He expressed through the striking of a parable. The seeker (the worshipper) and the sought (the one worshipped) are both weak.

﴿They did not revere God﴾ "magnified Him" ﴿as He truly deserves﴾ "in His greatness," when they associated with Him that which could not even defend itself against a fly, nor take revenge on it. ﴿Indeed God is Strong, Mighty﴾ "Victorious."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 75:

﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind.﴾ Messengers. It was revealed when the polytheists said, ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their saying, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He takes as a messenger, such as Jibril (Gabriel), Mikha'il (Michael), Ibrahim (Abraham), Muhammad and others, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 76:

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ i.e., what they have put forward, what they have left behind, what they have done, and what they will do afterwards.

O you who believe, bow down and prostrate yourselves, that is, pray, and worship your Lord, that is, make Him one (waḥḥidūhu), and do good, such as maintaining ties of kinship and noble moral conduct, so that you may prosper, that is, attain success by remaining forever in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 22, verse 78:

﴿And strive for Allah﴾ for the establishment of His religion, ﴿with the striving due to Him﴾ by exhausting one's capacity in it. The word ḥaqq is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿He chose you﴾ selected you for His religion. ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾ i.e., any narrowness, in that He made it easy during necessities, such as shortening the prayer (qaṣr), tayammum, eating carrion, and breaking the fast due to illness or travel. ﴿The religion of your father﴾ is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, the kāf, ﴿Ibrahim﴾ is an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān). ﴿He named you Muslims﴾ — ﴿He﴾ i.e., Allah — ﴿before﴾ i.e., before this Book, ﴿and in this﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection that he conveyed to you, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ that their messengers conveyed to them. ﴿So establish the prayer﴾ persist in it, ﴿and give the zakat, and hold fast to Allah﴾ trust in Him. ﴿He is your Master﴾ your Helper and the Manager of your affairs, ﴿so excellent is the Master﴾ He is, ﴿and excellent is the Helper﴾ the One who helps you.
